rules: Components take no className / style: all visuals come from the theme style (@skeinui/themes/<style> or your own). Lay out with Flex / Grid / Row / Col, or wrap in your own element.
Pass variants as values (variant, color, size, radius); the allowed values are listed per prop.
Controlled values use value / onValueChange; open state uses open / onOpenChange.
Props are data first (options, items, fields, columns); ReactNode / render props are the escape hatch.
Colors in your own CSS come from tokens: var(--ui-*), never hex values.
Put <ConfigProvider themeStyle mode> at the root: it writes the theme to <html>, so overlays portalled to <body> are themed.

Accordion.description:
Accordion: a stack of sections whose bodies expand and collapse under their title rows.
Compose `Accordion.Item` > `Accordion.Trigger` (the title row) + `Accordion.Panel` (the body); one item is open at a time
by default, `multiple` allows several. `value` / `onValueChange` (or `defaultValue`) hold the open items' values.
`variant` sets the look. For a single expand / collapse region use Collapsible.

Theme style: expand / collapse, keyboard navigation and aria wiring come from Base UI.

This prop is ignored when `hiddenUntilFound` is used.

AdminLayout.description:
Whole-page frame: `layout` chooses how header, navigation, tab bar, content and footer are arranged. Data-driven, knows nothing about routes:
navigation is a tree (`items`) plus the current item (`activeKey`); clicks are handed back via `onNavigate` and you navigate in the callback.

- `side`: the whole left column is the sidebar (logo, navigation), the right has tabs, content and footer. The toolbar (`actions`) is at the bottom of the sidebar by default, with no header;
  `toolbar="header"` moves it to the right of the header above the content area, with the breadcrumb on the left; when the toolbar is at the bottom of the sidebar, passing a breadcrumb also adds a header holding only the breadcrumb.
- `top`: the header holds the logo and primary navigation (items with children are dropdown menus), below are tabs, content and footer.
- `mix`: the header holds the logo and primary navigation; the sidebar shows the children of whichever item is selected.
- `column`: below the header, on the left is a primary icon column, next to it a column with the selected item's submenu (collapsible), then the content.
- `boxed`: the sidebar blends into the page background and the content is a rounded card.

Narrow screens (below md): the sidebar becomes a drawer; for top / mix / column the navigation moves into a drawer opened by the "open menu" button on the left of the header.
Reuses the library's `Sidebar`, `SideMenu`, `Menu`, `Drawer`; put `PageTabs` in the tab bar and `KeepAlive` in the content.

actions.description: Actions at the far right of the header (notifications, user menu...). The side layout has no header, so they go at the bottom of the sidebar.

activeKey.description: Key of the navigation item (leaf) for the current page; which top-level item is selected and which sidebar group is expanded are derived from it.

background.description: Boxed layout: the background behind the content card.

breadcrumb.description: Breadcrumb in the header (not every layout needs it).

breadcrumbIcons.description:
Header breadcrumb icons: `all` shows every item's (items with `BreadcrumbItem.icon`), `first` keeps only the first item's, `none` shows none.
Passed to the inner `Breadcrumb` via context (its own `icons` wins). Defaults to `settings.breadcrumbIcons`, then `all`.

breadcrumbSeparator.description: Header breadcrumb separator style: `chevron` small arrow, `slash` slash. Defaults to `settings.breadcrumbSeparator`, then `chevron`.

children.description: Page content. Use `KeepAlive` to keep pages that were navigated away from.

collapsed.description: Sidebar collapsed to an icon-only strip (side / mix / boxed); in the column layout it is the level-2 menu column collapsing. Controlled.

context.description: Context switcher next to the logo (tenant, workspace...). In the side layout it is below the logo.

footerFixed.description: Footer is fixed at the bottom (with a top border); otherwise it scrolls with the content.

items.description: Navigation tree. Data-driven: owned by the caller, the component knows nothing about routes.

labels.description: Built-in texts to override (see its Labels type below); by default they follow the ConfigProvider locale.

layout.description: Layout: `side`, `top`, `mix` (top level in the header, level 2 in the sidebar), `column` (an icon rail + a menu column) or `boxed` (the content is a rounded card). Defaults to `settings.layout`.

logo.description: Brand (logo + name). In the side layout it is at the top of the sidebar; in other layouts at the far left of the header.

logoMark.description: Small mark shown instead of `logo` when the sidebar collapses to a narrow strip (icon only, no name); without it `logo` is still shown. The context switcher is not shown in the strip.

maximized.description: Content area maximized: header, sidebar and navigation are hidden, leaving only the tabs, content and footer.

menuVariant.description: Navigation menu appearance: `default` is the theme style's own look; `modern` has taller items and a light primary background for the selected one (the console's "Sidebar style"). Defaults to `settings.menuVariant`.

onCollapsedChange.description: Called with the new `collapsed`; pass `collapsed` as well to control it.

onMaximizedChange.description:
When provided (and `tabs` is passed), a "maximize / restore" button appears on the right of the tab row (clicking calls it, and you update `maximized`). When maximized the header and
sidebar are hidden but the tab row stays, so the restore button is always reachable. Without a tab bar there is no button (as in the console: it is part of the tab bar).

onNavigate.type: (key: string, item: AdminNavItem, event: MouseEvent<HTMLElement, MouseEvent>) => void
onNavigate.description: A leaf was clicked (clicking a top-level item with children goes to its first child). For an item with `href` that you want to navigate yourself (router), call `event.preventDefault()` here.

onRefresh.description: When provided (and `tabs` is passed), a "refresh current page" button appears on the right of the tab row (together with `KeepAlive`'s `versions` it remounts the current page); without a tab bar there is none.

semiDark.description:
Semi Dark: when the page is in light mode, the navigation areas (sidebar, both columns of the column layout, header) are forced dark; the content area and tab bar are unchanged. `auto` (default) follows the theme style
(antd has a dark sidebar by default, others light), `on` dark, `off` light. Has no effect when the sidebar color is customized (`colors.sidebar` in `themeOverrides` decides),
or when the page itself is in dark mode.

settings.description:
An exported settings object (JSON exported by the `AdminLayoutSettings` panel, or the value of `useAdminLayoutSettings`): one prop applies layout, menu style and
theme; `tabs` is not rendered when `showTabs` is false. The individual props below (`layout`, `menuVariant`, `semiDark`) win when set.
The custom theme (primary / secondary / status colors / background / panel / sidebar color, radius, density) is also in `settings.themeOverrides`: colors are dynamic values and the component writes no style,
computing CSS variables and setting them on the element with a ref (recomputed when switching light/dark mode). See `themeVars`, `AdminLayoutSettings`.
The tab style (`tabVariant`) is a prop of your own `PageTabs` and the theme style belongs to `ConfigProvider`; neither is managed here.

tabs.description: A row above the content, usually holding `PageTabs`. On narrow screens a button to open the sidebar appears on its left.

themeScope.description:
Where the theme is written: `layout` (default) only applies inside AdminLayout; `document` writes to `<html>`, so overlays (menus, dialogs,
tooltips... rendered in a Portal, outside AdminLayout) change too; use it for a consistent look across the whole app.

toolbar.description: Position of the toolbar (`actions`) in the side layout: `sidebar` (bottom of the sidebar) or `header` (right of a header above the content). In other layouts `actions` are already in the header and unaffected. Defaults to `settings.toolbar`.

AdminLayoutColors.description: Customizable colors. All `#rrggbb`; those not given use the theme style's / theme's own values.

background.description: Page background. When a dark color is chosen, text, outline and neutral colors switch to light tones accordingly.

danger.description: Status color for errors and destructive actions.

field.description: Input background: when unset it follows the page background (changes with it), when set it is used on its own.

foreground.description: Text color: when not given, white or dark ink is chosen by the background's lightness; when given it is used, and secondary text, outline and neutral colors are all mixed from it and the background.

primary.description: Primary color: buttons, selected items, links, focus. Hover / pressed / outline are derived from it by the theme style.

sidebar.description: Sidebar background (in the column layout, the primary icon column and the level-2 menu column); text uses the contrast color, and a dark background puts the sidebar in dark mode (menu text turns light). The top layout has no sidebar and is unaffected.

success.description: Status color for success (alerts, badges, tags with `color="success"`).

surface.description:
Panel color: the base of containers such as cards, tables, code blocks, and of **overlays** (popover, dialog, dropdown menu); also the base of the sidebar (when no sidebar color is customized) and
the boxed frame (when no sidebar color is customized). When unset, overlays follow the theme style; when the background is dark and no panel color is set, overlays automatically take the background lightened a bit.

navigation.description: Name of the primary navigation (the top bar's navigation, the column layout's icon column).

openMenu.description: The header's "open menu" button on narrow screens.

refresh.description: Built-in buttons on the right of the tab row: refresh the current page, maximize / restore the content area.

subNavigation.description: Name of the level-2 menu in the column layout, and its collapse / expand button.

AdminLayoutSettingsValue.description: The full settings edited by the settings panel: arrangement (the layout items) plus appearance (theme). AdminLayout's props are taken directly from it.

breadcrumbIcons.description: Breadcrumb icons in the header: `all` shows every item's (those with an icon), `first` keeps only the first, `none` shows none. Unset equals `all`.

breadcrumbSeparator.description: Breadcrumb separator: `chevron` small arrow, `slash` slash. Unset equals `chevron`.

headerFollowsSidebar.description:
In the boxed layout, when the sidebar color is customized, whether the header and outer frame also use it (default yes, all three in one color). `false`: the header and frame keep the theme style's own base color.
Only affects boxed; in other layouts the header is part of the page and does not follow the sidebar.

semiDark.description:
Semi Dark: when the page is in light mode, the navigation areas (sidebar, both columns of the column layout, header) are forced dark. `auto` follows the theme style (antd has a dark sidebar by default, others light),
`on` dark, `off` light. Has no effect when the sidebar color is customized or the page itself is in dark mode. Unset equals `auto`.

showBreadcrumb.description: Whether to show the breadcrumb in the header (only meaningful for apps that pass `breadcrumb`). `false` hides it; unset means shown.

showTabs.description: Whether to show the page tabs bar (open pages) above the content.

themeOverrides.description: Custom layer: overrides colors / radius / density one by one on top of the theme style and color theme.

themeStyle.description:
Theme style id (`ConfigProvider`'s `themeStyle`). The library does not own `<html>` and does not know which styles the app imported:
the panel's "Theme style" section is fed by the app via `themeStyles`; once selected, pass it to `ConfigProvider themeStyle` to take effect. Unset means styles are not managed.

toolbar.description: Position of the toolbar (user, messages, light/dark toggle...) in the side layout (`side`): `sidebar` at the bottom of the sidebar (no header), `header` on the right of the header above the content area. Unset equals `sidebar`.

colors.description: Color overrides (`#rrggbb`) used in light mode, and in dark mode for items `dark` does not override.

dark.description:
Items that override `colors` in dark mode (used when the light and dark palettes are not derived from the same color: e.g. in dark the primary is brightened and the background is a different gray set).
Merged into `colors` only when the page is in dark mode; items not written keep `colors`.

density.description:
Density multiplier (1 = default, 0.8 compact, 1.3 loose): control height and width (horizontal padding, spacing, width of square controls) all scale with it.
Only effective for components that read `--ui-density` / `--ui-height-*` (theme styles are adding this one by one).

radius.description:
Three radius steps (rem). `radiusSm`: small things such as tags, checkboxes, kbd; `radius`: the md step, controls such as inputs, buttons, menu items, dropdowns;
`radiusLg`: large blocks such as cards, dialogs, drawers. If any of them is written, sm / md / lg and the radius roles the components read use this set directly,
no longer going through the theme style's own conversion, so the same number means the same thing in any theme style (but heroui's pill controls stay pills, that is their form).
When only some are written, the missing ones are derived from md: sm = md × 0.5, lg = md × 1.5. When none is written, the theme style is used as is.

radiusLg.description: Large radius step (rem): cards, dialogs, drawers. See `radius`.

radiusSm.description: Small radius step (rem): tags, checkboxes, kbd. See `radius`.

AdminNavItem.description: One navigation item: a leaf (navigates on click) or a group with `children`. Same shape as `SideMenuItem` (but without group / divider).

disabled.description: Disables interaction.

href.description: When provided it renders as a link `<a>`; to handle navigation yourself (router), call `event.preventDefault()` in `onNavigate`.

icon.description: Leading icon; when the sidebar collapses to a strip and in the column layout's icon column, only it remains.

key.description: Unique key; matched against AdminLayout's `activeKey` and passed to `onNavigate`.

label.description: Menu text.

title.description: Tooltip text and accessible name when only the icon is shown; may be omitted when `label` is a string.

examples.title: Usage
examples.code:
<AdminLayout
  layout="side"
  items={items}
  activeKey={activeKey}
  onNavigate={(key, item, event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    navigate(key); // your own router
  }}
  logo={<Logo />}
  context={<TenantSwitcher />}
  actions={<UserMenu />}
  tabs={<PageTabs tabs={tabs} activeKey={activeKey} … />}
  footer="© 2026 Skein UI"
>
  <KeepAlive activeKey={activeKey} keepKeys={tabs.map((t) => t.key)}>
    <Page />
  </KeepAlive>
</AdminLayout>

Affix.description:
Affix: pins an element (a toolbar, a bottom action bar) to the edge of the scroll container when it would scroll out of view.
Pinned at `offsetTop` (or `offsetBottom`), it is released when it is back in place;
the page does not jump. `target` is the scroll container (the window by default), `onChange` reports pin / release.

Theme style: when pinned, the content is `position: fixed` with a same-size placeholder left in place. A ref sets
--affix-top / --affix-left / --affix-w / --affix-h on the root (pixels, no unit); the theme style applies them and the layering.
When an ancestor has a transform, the component measures the offset and compensates.

offsetBottom.description: Pixels from the container bottom at which to pin (for when the element is below the container and only comes into view after scrolling, e.g. a bottom action bar); when given, the top is no longer used.

offsetTop.description: Pixels from the container top at which to pin. Defaults to 0 when offsetBottom is not given.

target.description: Scroll container to watch: an element, a ref, or a function returning one. Defaults to the window.

Agenda.description:
Calendar of events with day, week and month views, navigation and optional drag-to-reschedule.
Pass `events` (`AgendaEvent[]`: `id`, `title`, `start` / `end` as "YYYY-MM-DD" or "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm", no time zone); events are owned by the caller.
`view` / `onViewChange` and `date` / `onDateChange` control the view and the day shown (or use the uncontrolled defaults).
The day and week views are timelines (all-day / multi-day bars on top, timed events placed by time, overlapping ones side by side, a current time line today);
the month view has one week per row, and events that do not fit collapse into "+n more" (`onMoreClick`, or it switches to that day).
`onEventClick` / `onSlotClick` report clicks; passing `onEventChange` enables dragging and Alt + arrow keys to move / resize events.
For picking a date use Calendar or DatePicker.

Theme style: positions and sizes are numbers only known at runtime, written as CSS variables with a ref: --ev-start / --ev-length (minutes), --ev-col / --ev-cols
(overlap columns), --seg-col / --seg-span / --seg-row (event bars in a row), converted to lengths by the theme style.

date.description: The day the view is centered on, "YYYY-MM-DD", controlled; the week view shows the week containing it, the month view the month containing it.

defaultDate.description: Initial `date` when uncontrolled; today when not given.

In-page table of contents: clicking a link scrolls to its section, and the section in view is highlighted while scrolling.
Pass `items` (`href: "#id"`, `title`, nested `children`); `direction` lays it out vertically or as a horizontal row,
`container` sets the scroll container, `offset` accounts for a fixed top bar, and `value` / `onValueChange` control the highlighted link (computed from scrolling when not passed).
For page-to-page navigation use Breadcrumb, Tabs or Link.

a ref sets the current link's position relative to the root as --anchor-x / --anchor-y / --anchor-w / --anchor-h (pixels, no unit),
which the theme style uses for positioning and the sliding animation.

Round (or `radius`-shaped) picture of a user or entity, with a text fallback such as initials.
Pass `src` and `alt`; `fallback` is shown while there is no image or when it fails to load. `size` / `color` / `radius` set the look,

BorderBeam.description:
Border beam: adds a continuously flowing decorative highlight around a container's border (login panel, recommendation card, AI module, key CTA).
Purely decorative, `aria-hidden` and does not intercept the mouse; it does not replace the border of focus, validation or business states.

A beam is a string of small segments running along the rounded rectangle border (SVG stroke-dash, each with its own color and opacity),
so at corners the tail bends along, rather than a whole square gradient suddenly covering two edges at once at a corner.
Drawing and animation live in the theme style; the component only measures the container and writes values as CSS variables; the whole layer is hidden when the system asks for reduced motion.

color.description: Beam color: a single color string, or an array of gradient stops (the first is at the head of the beam). Uses the primary color if not given.

count.description: Number of beams, evenly distributed along the border.

duration.description: Time (seconds) for a beam to complete one lap.

fit.description:
The container hugs the content's size (buttons, badges, avatars and the like). By default the container fills the available width like a block (cards, panels),
and in a horizontal flex it is also stretched to the same height as its neighbors, so the beam leaves the content's border; turn on `fit` for such cases.

outset.description: Distance (pixels) the beam layer extends outward from the container edge.

radius.description: Border radius; it must match the wrapped content (the beam is drawn along it).

size.description: Length of the beam (head to tail), in pixels.

trigger.description: `always` flows all the time, `hover` shows only when the mouse is over / focus enters.

color.description: Any CSS color of this stop (e.g. "#7c3aed", "var(--ui-primary)").

percent.description: 0–100: position of the gradient stop within the visible beam segment; a transparent transition is left at the tail.

  { color: "#36cfc9", percent: 52 },
  { color: "#95de64", percent: 100 },
]}>…</BorderBeam>

Combobox.description:
Searchable single-select: type in the input to filter the options, then pick one; the value must be one of the options.
Pass `options` (`{ value, label }`, or groups `{ label, options }`), and `value` / `onValueChange` (a string, null when nothing is selected);
`emptyText` is shown when nothing matches. For a short list without typing use Select; when free text is allowed and options are only suggestions use Autocomplete.

so the two are automatically consistent in every theme style. Filtering, keyboard navigation and accessibility come from Base UI's Combobox.

Command.description:
Command palette shown inline: a search box over a list of commands that filters and ranks them as you type.
Pass `items` (commands, optionally in `{ type: "group" }` groups) and handle `onSelect(key, item)`; each item can also
carry its own `onSelect`, `icon`, `shortcut` hint and search `keywords`. The search term is internal unless you pass
`query` / `onQueryChange`. Focus stays in the input: ↑ ↓ move (wrapping), Home / End, Enter runs (not during IME
composition). For a popup palette opened by a hotkey use CommandDialog; to pick a value in a form use Combobox or Autocomplete.

disabled rows `data-disabled`.

(`ToolbarStart` / `ToolbarEnd`, `Composer.Action`, `Composer.Send`); `Composer.Footer` is a note below.
For a plain multi-line form field use Textarea; for

ConfigProvider.description:
App-wide settings provider, placed once at the app root: picks the theme style, light / dark mode, color theme and
density, and supplies the default locale and UI text to every component inside.
Pass `themeStyle` (e.g. "antd"), `mode` ("light" / "dark" / "system"), `themeColor`, `themeDensity`, per-item
`themeOverrides` (colors, radii, density), `locale` (BCP 47) for date components and `labels` (a stable object) to
translate component text; a component's own `locale` / `labels` win. Omitted settings are left untouched, and changing
one does not remount the subtree.

Theme style: settings are written to `<html>` as `data-skein-theme` / `data-skein-mode` / `data-skein-color` /
`data-skein-density` (on `<html>` so portalled overlays follow), `themeOverrides` as inline CSS variables on `<html>`;
previous values are restored on unmount or change.

labels.description: Text of the components, replaced as a whole when changing language; `labels` passed by the component itself takes precedence. Pass a stable reference, do not create the object inline in render.

locale.description: Default locale for date components (BCP 47, e.g. "zh-CN"); a `locale` passed by the component itself takes precedence.

mode.description: Light / dark, written to `<html data-skein-mode>`; "system" follows the OS and updates when the OS switches.

themeColor.description: Color theme (colors only, both light and dark sets), written to `<html data-skein-color>`; multiple can be passed, joined with spaces.

themeDensity.description: Density (e.g. "compact"), written to `<html data-skein-density>`; if omitted, it is the theme style's own density.

themeOverrides.description:
Per-item overrides on top of theme style / color theme / density: colors, three border radius levels (`radiusSm / radius / radiusLg`, rem), density multiplier, and
the same data as `settings.themeOverrides` of `AdminLayout` (this is what the settings panel exports). Written to inline CSS variables on `<html>`
(overlays follow too), restored on unmount or change; colors are recomputed when switching light / dark mode.

themeStyle.description: Theme style (shape, density baseline, fonts, component look), written to `<html data-skein-theme>`.

AdminLayoutColors.description: Customizable colors. All `#rrggbb`; those not given use the theme style's / theme's own values.

background.description: Page background. When a dark color is chosen, text, outline and neutral colors switch to light tones accordingly.

danger.description: Status color for errors and destructive actions.

field.description: Input background: when unset it follows the page background (changes with it), when set it is used on its own.

foreground.description: Text color: when not given, white or dark ink is chosen by the background's lightness; when given it is used, and secondary text, outline and neutral colors are all mixed from it and the background.

primary.description: Primary color: buttons, selected items, links, focus. Hover / pressed / outline are derived from it by the theme style.

sidebar.description: Sidebar background (in the column layout, the primary icon column and the level-2 menu column); text uses the contrast color, and a dark background puts the sidebar in dark mode (menu text turns light). The top layout has no sidebar and is unaffected.

success.description: Status color for success (alerts, badges, tags with `color="success"`).

surface.description:
Panel color: the base of containers such as cards, tables, code blocks, and of **overlays** (popover, dialog, dropdown menu); also the base of the sidebar (when no sidebar color is customized) and
the boxed frame (when no sidebar color is customized). When unset, overlays follow the theme style; when the background is dark and no panel color is set, overlays automatically take the background lightened a bit.

colors.description: Color overrides (`#rrggbb`) used in light mode, and in dark mode for items `dark` does not override.

dark.description:
Items that override `colors` in dark mode (used when the light and dark palettes are not derived from the same color: e.g. in dark the primary is brightened and the background is a different gray set).
Merged into `colors` only when the page is in dark mode; items not written keep `colors`.

density.description:
Density multiplier (1 = default, 0.8 compact, 1.3 loose): control height and width (horizontal padding, spacing, width of square controls) all scale with it.
Only effective for components that read `--ui-density` / `--ui-height-*` (theme styles are adding this one by one).

radius.description:
Three radius steps (rem). `radiusSm`: small things such as tags, checkboxes, kbd; `radius`: the md step, controls such as inputs, buttons, menu items, dropdowns;
`radiusLg`: large blocks such as cards, dialogs, drawers. If any of them is written, sm / md / lg and the radius roles the components read use this set directly,
no longer going through the theme style's own conversion, so the same number means the same thing in any theme style (but heroui's pill controls stay pills, that is their form).
When only some are written, the missing ones are derived from md: sm = md × 0.5, lg = md × 1.5. When none is written, the theme style is used as is.

radiusLg.description: Large radius step (rem): cards, dialogs, drawers. See `radius`.

radiusSm.description: Small radius step (rem): tags, checkboxes, kbd. See `radius`.

ConfigLabels.description: Text passed to ConfigProvider: for each component and each entry, you can write only what you want to change.

const labels = { pagination: { next: "Next page" } }; // module level, so the reference is stable

<ConfigProvider themeStyle="antd" mode="system" themeColor="contrast" locale="zh-CN" labels={labels}>
  <App />
</ConfigProvider>

DataTable.description:
A table from data: `columns` and `rows`, with the loading and empty states, an optional checkbox column
(`selected` / `onSelectedChange`), sorting (`sort` / `onSortChange`) and an actions column (`actions`) whose buttons
can ask for confirmation first. It is the table of a list page, ready made; for anything beyond it (expandable rows,
editable cells, a footer), use `Table` and its parts.

Theme style: it is Table, Checkbox, Button and Popconfirm and has no slot of its own.

actions.type: (row: Row, index: number) => readonly (false | DataTableAction | null | undefined)[]
actions.description:
The actions of a row, in order. Falsy entries are skipped, so a permission reads naturally:
`(row) => [can("edit") && { key: "edit", label: "Edit", onClick: … }]`. A row with none has an empty cell.

empty.description: What the table says when there are no rows; defaults to the locale's "No data".

loading.description: The table is loading: the body fades and cannot be clicked; with no rows, the empty row says "Loading…".

onSelectedChange.description: Called with the new `selected`; pass `selected` as well to control it.

onSortChange.description:
A sort button was clicked: the next sort, which goes ascending, then descending, then (`null`) back to none.
Sorting the rows (or asking the server to) is yours.

rowKey.type: (keyof Row & string) | ((row: Row, index: number) => string)
rowKey.description: A row's identity: the name of a field holding a string or a number, or a function.

selected.description: Keys of the selected rows; giving it (with `onSelectedChange`) adds the checkbox column.

sort.description: The column the rows are sorted by, and how.

stickyHeader.description: Keep the header in view and scroll only the rows: the table fills the height of its parent, which has to be constrained (a box with a height, or a flex column that has one: `Card fill`, `Flex grow`). Without it the table is as tall as its rows and the page scrolls.

align.description: Horizontal alignment of the header and the cells.

fixed.description: Sticks to the left (start) or right (end) edge while the table scrolls sideways.

key.description: Identifies the column (the key of its cells and of the sort); also the field of the row shown when there is no `render`.

render.description: What the cell shows for a row; without it, the row's field named `key` as text (a string, a number or a boolean; anything else needs a `render`).

sortable.description: The header gets a sort button; the sort itself is yours (`sort` / `onSortChange`).

title.description: Text of the header.

width.description: Column width (px): once set, this column has a fixed width.

Actions

<DataTable
  rows={rows}

DatePicker.description:
Form field that opens a calendar popup to pick a date, a week / month / quarter / year (`picker`), a date with time (`showTime`) or a range (`mode="range"`).
Values are strings: "YYYY-MM-DD" (or "YYYY-MM", "YYYY-Qn", "YYYY", "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm"); a range is `{ start, end }`. Use `value` / `onValueChange`,
limit choices with `min` / `max` / `isDateDisabled`, and set `editable` to let users type the date. Single selection closes once a date is picked,
range selection after the end date is picked (with `showTime`, on "OK" or clicking outside).
For an always-visible calendar use Calendar; for a time of day only use TimePicker.

Theme style: the trigger reuses Select's look (slot is select-trigger), the popup reuses Popover with a Calendar inside.

Dialog.description:
Modal window over the page for a focused task or message: `<Dialog.Trigger>` opens `<Dialog.Content>`, which holds `Dialog.Title`, `Dialog.Description`,
`Dialog.Body` and `Dialog.Footer` (put `Dialog.Close` or your buttons there). `open` / `onOpenChange` control it; Esc, the close button
(`closeButton`, on by default) and clicking the backdrop close it, focus stays inside while open, and `size` sets the width.
For a yes / no confirmation use ConfirmDialog or AlertDialog; for a panel sliding in from an edge use Drawer; for non-modal floating content use Popover.

Theme style: focus trapping, Esc to close and background scroll lock all come from Base UI.

Call `preventUnmountOnClose()` in `onOpenChange` first, otherwise the dialog completes closing on its own.
Whether it leaves the DOM is decided by `keepMounted` on the portal.
- `close`: Closes the dialog imperatively when called.

with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

value.description: The value of the input. Use when controlled.

Kanban.description:
Kanban board: several columns of cards, and cards can be dragged between columns and reordered within a column. The data is flat `columns` + `cards` (cards have a `columnId`,
and the array order is the order within the column), the state is held by the caller: after a drag the new array is handed back via `onCardsChange`.
While dragging, the card lands at its new position live (preview), and the notification comes only on release, Esc cancels; keyboard: after focusing a card, Alt + Left / Right changes column, Alt + Up / Down changes order,
each announced with `role="status"`, with focus staying on this card. Card content is a fixed set of items (title, description, tags, progress, footer).

cards.description: Flat cards, each with a `columnId`; the array order is the order within the column.

collapsible.description: The column header menu has "Collapse": a collapsed column is a narrow strip with a vertical title, click the button on it to expand; cards can still be dragged in (landing at the end).

columns.description: The columns, left to right (`KanbanColumn`: `id`, `title`, `color`); owned by the caller.

height.description:
Height of the board (a number is px, or a length such as `"calc(100vh - 12rem)"`). If given: each column is at most this tall,
the column header and "Add" are fixed, the cards in between scroll within the column, and the whole board only scrolls horizontally (like Trello); if not given: columns grow with their content.

labels.description: Built-in texts to override (see its Labels type below); by default they follow the ConfigProvider locale.

onAddCard.description:
If given, an "Add card" appears at the bottom of each column: clicking shows an input in place at the bottom of the column, Enter adds (the input stays so you can keep typing), Esc collapses it.
The callback gives which column and what the title is; the caller creates the card (id, etc.) and adds it to `cards`.

onAddColumn.description: If given, "Add another column" appears at the end of the board: clicking shows an input in place, Enter adds; the caller creates the column and adds it to `columns`.

onCardClick.description: If given, a card is a button (Enter opens it); if not given (and `onCardEdit` is not given either) it is a plain block.

onCardDelete.description:
If given, pressing the `Delete` key while a card is focused, or clicking "Delete" in the edit dialog (requires `onCardEdit` as well), first shows a confirmation, and after confirming it is called.
**The caller must remove the card** (remove it from `cards`); the component does not delete it for you.

onCardEdit.description:
If given, clicking a card (Enter / Space also work) opens an edit dialog (like Trello): edit title and description, Enter / Save submits, Esc / Cancel discards.
An empty title cannot be saved, and no notification if nothing changed. The caller updates `cards`. If `onCardClick` is also given, both are triggered.

onCardMove.description: Same as above, but gives the before and after positions of this move (for syncing to a backend).

onCardsChange.description: After a card is dragged / moved by keyboard, gives the whole array after the move; just update `cards` with it. It must be passed for dragging to work.

onCollapsedColumnsChange.description: Called with the new `collapsedColumns`; pass `collapsedColumns` as well to control it.

onColumnDelete.description:
If given, the column header menu has "Delete": clicking first shows a confirmation, and after confirming it is called. **The caller must remove both the column and its cards**
(remove the column from `columns` and its cards from `cards`); the component does not delete them for you.

onColumnMove.description: Same as above, but gives the before and after positions of this move.

onColumnRename.description: If given, the column header menu has "Rename" (double-clicking the column title also works): after editing it gives the new title, and the caller updates `columns`.

onColumnsChange.description: After a column is dragged / moved by keyboard, gives the whole array after the move; just update `columns` with it. If passed, dragging a column header reorders the columns.

size.description: Levels for column width and gap: sm 240px, md 280px, lg 320px (decided by the theme style).

columnId.description: Which column it is in. The order in the array is the order within that column.

description.description: Secondary text under the title.

footer.description: Custom content at the bottom of the card (avatars, comment count, ...). Do not put buttons / links in it: the whole card is one focusable, draggable block.

id.description: Unique id across the board, stable while the card moves.

labels.description: A row of small tags below the title.

progress.description: Progress (0–100): the progress bar is shown if given.

title.description: Card heading.

color.description: Color of the status dot in the column header; neutral if not given.

id.description: Unique id; cards point to it with `columnId`.

title.description: Column heading.

color.description: Semantic colour; the theme style picks the actual colours.

label.description: Tag text.

add.description: Text of the "Add" button at the bottom of a column.

addCardLabel.description: Inline "add card" input: name, placeholder, submit button, and the announcement after adding.

addColumn.description: "Add column" at the end of the board: button text, plus the inline input's name, placeholder, submit button and the announcement after adding.

board.description: Name of the board, default "Kanban board".

colors.description: Names of tag colors (screen reader names of the swatches).

column.description: Name of each column: title and card count.

columnHint.description: Hint for keyboard moves of a column (read by screen readers on the column).

columnMenu.description: Name of the column header menu button.

columnMoved.type: (title: string, position: number, total: number) => string
columnMoved.description: Announcement after a column is moved: which column, and how many in total.

deleteCardTitle.description: Confirmation for deleting a card: title, description, and the announcement after deleting. Button text uses `delete`.

deleteDescription.description: Description for the delete confirmation: the column name and the number of cards in it.

editCardTitle.description: Title of the edit dialog, and the "which column" description under the title.

editLabels.description: Names of the tags, progress and footer items in the edit dialog.

editTitleLabel.description: Names of the two inputs in the edit box.

empty.description: Message in a column with no cards.

expand.description: Name of the "expand" button on the narrow strip of a collapsed column.

hint.description: Hint for keyboard moves (read by screen readers on the card).

moved.type: (title: string, column: string, position: number, total: number) => string
moved.description: Announcement after a card is moved: the new column, which card, and how many in total.

/>

KeepAlive.description:
Keep-alive: keeps visited pages in memory (hidden rather than unmounted), so state, typed content and scroll position are still there when you switch back.
Unrelated to routing: you tell it which item is current (`activeKey`) and that item's content (`children`), and it keeps and hides them.
Hiding uses React's `Activity`: state is preserved, but effects (subscriptions, timers) are paused and resumed on return.

Each item lives in its own pane (`overflow: auto`) that scrolls itself: browsers discard the scroll position of hidden elements, and here it is restored when shown again.
Deeper scroll containers inside the page are not handled; the page must handle them itself if they need to be kept.

activeKey.description: Which item is currently shown (e.g. the current route path, the current tab key).

children.description: Content of the current item. After switching away, the item keeps **the last content it received** and is no longer updated.

keepKeys.description:
Keys of the items to keep (e.g. the currently open tabs). Items not in it are dropped and their state is cleared: close a tab and its page is gone.
If not given, all visited items are kept (limited by `max`). The current item is unaffected by it and is always shown.

max.description: Maximum number of items kept at once; when exceeded, the least recently viewed is dropped. Unlimited by default.

transition.description: Enter animation when switching to an item; the style is decided by the theme style; none under "reduced motion".

versions.description: To make an item start over (refresh): increment its number by 1 and it will be remounted.

Layout.description:
Page skeleton: put Header / Content / Footer vertically inside Layout; Layout can also be nested.
For an app shell with a sidebar use `Sidebar`. The root Layout sets no height itself; it fills only when given a definite height from outside (e.g. a `100vh` container).

Link.description:
Link: an inline text link (`href`), with `color` / `variant`; `external` opens it in a new tab.
To integrate with a router, do not use the render prop: wrap the router's <Link>, or call the router navigation in onClick.
For an action that doesn't navigate use Button (`variant="ghost"`).

color.description: Semantic colour; the theme style picks the actual colours.

disabled.description: Removes `href`, so the link can't be followed.

external.description: External link: opens in a new window with rel="noopener noreferrer"; the theme style may append an external-link icon.

variant.description: `default` is always coloured; `subtle` uses the text colour with a faint underline and takes the colour on hover.

examples.title: Usage

<Link href="/docs">Read the docs</Link>

List.description:

Semantically `<li>` inside `<ul>`; `aria-busy` is set while loading. For row and column alignment like a table use Table, not this.

bordered.description: Outer border + left and right padding of items.

empty.description: Content shown when there are no items: a string is shown in an `Empty`, a node as it is. Defaults to the locale's "No data".

footer.description: Content below the items (e.g. a "Load more" button).

header.description: Content above the items (e.g. a heading or toolbar).

items.description: Data-driven: each item is the props of `List.Item` plus a `key`. Can be omitted, and you put `List.Item` as children yourself.

loading.description: Loading: the list fades, becomes unclickable, and a spinner is shown in the middle.

actions.description: Actions on the far right (links, buttons), with separators added between them automatically.

description.description: Secondary text under the title.

extra.description: Extra content on the right (time, status, thumbnail).

title.description: Main line of the item.

description.description: Secondary text under the title.

extra.description: Extra content on the right (time, status, thumbnail).

key.description: Unique key of the item (React key).

title.description: Main line of the item.

LoginLayout.description:
The page around a sign-in (or sign-up) form: three looks for the same parts. The brand, the title and the form are
the page's own, this only places them; the soft glow and the dividers come from the theme style.

Theme style: `--ui-login-min-height` (default the viewport's height) sets how tall the page is, e.g. to show it
inside a box.

backgroundImage.description: `cover`: a picture for the whole page instead of the soft glow.

brand.description: The app's mark and name: part of the app, not of the page's text, so it stays the same in every language.

cover.description:
`split`: what the cover shows in its middle, under the brand and over the soft glow. Without it: a drawing with
`coverTitle` and `coverDescription` under it; `null` for nothing.

coverTitle.description: `split`: the tagline under the default drawing.

description.description: A line under the title.

footer.description: A hint, links, the copyright: under the form, and in `split` at the bottom of the form's side.

providers.description: Other ways in, under the form behind a divider.

variant.description:
`centered`: the form in a card in the middle; `split`: a cover on the left, the form on the right (wide screens only);
`cover`: the card over a full-page background. How each one looks is up to the theme style.

LoginLayoutProvider.description: One "continue with …" way in, shown as a button under the form.

icon.description: Usually the provider's logo.

id.description: Reported to `onProvider` when its button is pressed.

</LoginLayout>

  …
/>

Markdown.description:
Markdown rendering: a zero-dependency parser (headings, paragraphs, fenced code, quotes, lists / task lists, tables, horizontal rules,
inline code / bold / italic / strikethrough / links / images), with fenced code using `CodeBlock`.
HTML is not recognized and is treated as plain text; links and images only allow http(s) / mailto / tel and relative addresses.

breaks.description: A single newline within a paragraph also breaks the line (common in chat); by default it is treated as a space per the standard.

children.description: Raw Markdown. When streaming, just keep appending: earlier unchanged blocks are not redrawn, and unclosed markers are shown as raw text.

citations.description:
Citation sources: `[1]`, `[2]` in the body become clickable citation badges, and the nth source corresponds to `[n]` (1-based).
Numbers with no matching source (e.g. `[7]`) remain plain text. Pass stable citations: if the array changes, all blocks are redrawn.

codeRenderers.description:
Take over rendering of fenced code by language, e.g. `{ mermaid: ({ code }) => <MermaidBlock code={code} render={render} /> }`.
Not called while the fence is not yet closed (halfway through streaming); it is shown as a normal code block first. Pass a stable object: if it changes, all blocks are redrawn.

codeTheme.description: Theme of fenced code, same as `CodeBlock`'s `theme`.

highlight.type: boolean | ((code: string, language: string | undefined) => ReactNode[])
highlight.description: Highlighting of fenced code, same as `CodeBlock`'s `highlight`.

labels.description: Built-in texts to override (see its Labels type below); by default they follow the ConfigProvider locale.

math.description:
Math: when given, `$$…$$` blocks and inline `$…$`, `\\(…\\)`, `\\[…\\]` are recognized, and rendering is handed to this function (hook up KaTeX / MathJax),
which returns the content to put in the page. When not given, they are treated as plain text. The `$` rules are the same as Pandoc
(the opening `$` must not be followed by whitespace, the closing `$` must not be preceded by whitespace nor followed by a digit, so "$5 and $10" is not a formula);
an unclosed block formula (halfway through streaming) is shown as plain text first. Pass a stable function: if it changes, all blocks are redrawn.
If the function throws, the raw formula text is shown instead.

streaming.description: Still streaming: a blinking cursor is shown after the last piece of text and removed when finished.

description.description: When a description is given, hover / focus shows a preview card (title, description, domain).

faviconUrl.description: Address of the site icon (not fetched automatically); if missing or failing to load, shows the first letter of the title.

href.description: Link of the source (url sources), opened in a new tab (`noopener noreferrer`); non-http(s) addresses do not become links.

onClick.description: When a document source is clicked (e.g. to open a document preview).

sourceType.description: url: web source (default, when href is given), document: an uploaded document.

title.description: Displayed title, defaults to the link's domain.

table.description: Name of the table scroll area, default "Table".

taskDone.description: Screen-reader text for completed items in a task list, default "Completed".

Marquee.description:
Horizontal strip that scrolls its content continuously, for logos, tickers and announcements; it scrolls only when the content is wider than the container, otherwise it is static.
`speed` (px / s) and `direction` set the motion; it pauses on hover / focus (`pauseOnHover`) and has a pause button (`pausable`, keep it on for WCAG 2.2.2),
`paused` / `onPausedChange` control pausing. It does not scroll when the system requests reduced motion (the content becomes manually scrollable instead).
For paging through slides one at a time use Carousel.

Theme style: a copy of the content is duplicated end to end (hidden from screen readers and not focusable). The animation itself lives in the theme style;
the component only supplies the duration (--marquee-duration).

aria-label.description: Name of the region, used by screen readers.

direction.description: start scrolls toward the start direction (right to left, reversed under RTL), end is the opposite.

labels.description: Built-in texts to override (see its Labels type below); by default they follow the ConfigProvider locale.

onPausedChange.description: Called with the new `paused`; pass `paused` as well to control it.

pausable.description: Show a pause button. WCAG 2.2.2: automatically scrolling content lasting over 5 seconds must be pausable; do not turn it off unless an equivalent control exists elsewhere.

pauseOnHover.description: Pause on mouse hover / when focus is inside.

speed.description: Scroll speed, pixels / second: the duration is the content width / speed, written as `--marquee-duration`.

Masonry.description:
Multi-column layout where each item goes into the shortest column, so content of uneven height (images, cards) packs tightly.
Pass `items` (`{ key, data, height?, column? }`) with `itemRender`, or write the items as children; `columns` and `gutter` take a number or per-breakpoint values.
It re-lays out when the width changes or an item's height changes (e.g. an image finished loading); DOM order is the item order, so keyboard and screen readers follow it.
For equal-height rows use the Row / Col grid.

Theme style: positions are written as CSS variables (`--ms-col` / `--ms-y`) from numbers the component measured; horizontal position and width are computed by CSS from the column count,
so when the window gets wider or narrower the column width follows immediately and heights are laid out again; height changes of items (images finished loading) also trigger a re-layout.
Content is hidden before layout, so server rendering does not flash a pile of overlapping items. DOM order is the item order, and keyboard and screen readers follow it.

aria-label.description: Name of the whole list, used by screen readers.

children.description: The items, written directly (when `items` isn't given).

columns.description: Number of columns; can be given per breakpoint.

gutter.description: Gap between items (pixels, any value outside the theme style's scale): one number covers both horizontal and vertical, `[horizontal, vertical]` sets them separately; can be given per breakpoint.

itemRender.description: Render one item: when data-driven, use it to draw `item.data`.

items.description: Data-driven items; can be omitted, and you write each item directly as children.

onLayoutChange.type: (layout: { key: string | number; column: number; }[]) => void
onLayoutChange.description: After each layout, which column each item landed in.

children.description: Content of the item; takes precedence over `itemRender`.

column.description: Pinned to a column index (0-based); if not given it goes into the shortest column at that moment.

data.description: Your own stored data, passed to `itemRender`.

height.description: Content height (pixels), used to estimate positions before the first layout; afterwards the measured value is used.

key.description: Unique key of the item; also reported in `onLayoutChange`.

Mentions.description:
Mentions: typing a trigger character (default `@`) in the input pops up a candidate list next to the caret, and selecting one inserts the content into the text.
The input is still Input / Textarea with focus always staying inside it, and the list is read the combobox way (aria-activedescendant).
The value is just plain text; if the consumer wants to know who was mentioned, it parses the text by prefix itself.

aria-label.description: Accessible name, when there is no visible label.

aria-labelledby.description: Id of the element whose text names it.

disabled.description: Disables interaction.

filterOption.description: Filter rule; by default case-insensitive containment match against value and string label. false means no filtering (candidates are supplied by the consumer).

fullWidth.description: Fills the width of the parent.

multiline.description: Multi-line input (textarea); false is a single-line input.

name.description: Field name, for native form submission.

onSearch.description: Callback when the text after typing @ changes; use it when candidates are fetched from the server, and set filterOption to false at the same time.

onSelect.description: Callback when a candidate is selected; prefix is the character that triggered it.

onValueChange.description: Called with the new `value`; pass `value` as well to control it.

options.description: Candidates; when there are only names you can pass a string array directly.

prefix.description: Trigger characters; can give several, such as ["@", "#"].

readOnly.description: Text can be selected and copied but not edited; no candidate list opens (nor does it when disabled).

rows.description: Visible text rows of the textarea (only with `multiline`).

side.description: Whether the candidate list appears above or below the caret.

split.description: Characters appended after the inserted content on selection.

value.description: The value, controlled (with `onValueChange`).

variant.description: Visual variant; how each one looks is up to the theme style.

disabled.description: Disables interaction.

label.description: Content shown in the list, defaults to value; can be a node such as an avatar.

value.description: Content inserted into the text after selection (the part after the prefix).

examples.code:
import { Mentions } from "@skeinui/ui";

<Mentions aria-label="Message" placeholder="Type @ to mention" options={["Ada", "Alan", "Grace"]} />

examples.title: Controlled
examples.code:
<Mentions
  value={text}
  onValueChange={setText}
  onSelect={(option, prefix) => setLast(prefix + option.value)}
  options={[...]}
/>

Menu.description:
Dropdown list of actions opened from a trigger button: `<Menu.Trigger>` opens `<Menu.Content>`, which holds `Menu.Item`s (`onClick`, `color="danger"`),
`Menu.CheckboxItem`, `Menu.Group` + `Menu.GroupLabel` and `Menu.Separator`. `open` / `onOpenChange` control it; choosing an item or pressing Esc closes it,
and arrow keys and first-letter jump move through the items. For choosing a form value use Select; for a right-click menu use ContextMenu; for an app menu bar use Menubar.

Theme style: arrow keys, first-letter jump, Esc to close and collision flipping all come from Base UI.

actionsRef.description:
A ref to imperative actions.
- `unmount`: Ends the closing phase of the menu after an externally controlled closing animation finishes.
  Call `preventUnmountOnClose()` in `onOpenChange` first, otherwise the menu completes closing on its own.
  Whether it leaves the DOM is decided by `keepMounted` on the portal.
- `close`: Closes the menu imperatively when called.

children.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | PayloadChildRenderFunction<unknown>
children.description:
The content of the menu.
This can be a regular React node or a render function that receives the `payload` of the active trigger.

closeParentOnEsc.description:
When in a submenu, determines whether pressing the Escape key
closes the entire menu, or only the current child menu.

defaultOpen.description:
Whether the menu is initially open.

To render a controlled menu, use the `open` prop instead.

defaultTriggerId.description:
ID of the trigger that the menu is associated with.
This is useful in conjunction with the `defaultOpen` prop to create an initially open menu.

disabled.description: Whether the component should ignore user interaction.

handle.description:
A handle to associate the menu with a trigger.
If specified, allows external triggers to control the menu's open state.

highlightItemOnHover.description:
Whether moving the pointer over items should highlight them.
Disabling this prop allows CSS `:hover` to be differentiated from the `:focus` (`data-highlighted`) state.

loopFocus.description:
Whether to loop keyboard focus back to the first item
when the end of the list is reached while using the arrow keys.

modal.description:
Determines if the menu enters a modal state when open.
- `true`: user interaction is limited to the menu: document page scroll is locked and pointer interactions on outside elements are disabled.
- `false`: user interaction with the rest of the document is allowed.

On touch devices, a `true` modal blocks outside taps but leaves the page scrollable unless the popup spans nearly the full viewport width, matching native iOS behavior.

Nested menus ignore this prop, and menus opened by hover are never modal.

onItemHighlighted.description:
Callback fired when an item is highlighted or unhighlighted.
Receives the highlighted item element (or `undefined` if no item is highlighted) and details
containing the reason for the change, the event, and the item's text label.
The `reason` can be:
- `'keyboard'`: the highlight changed due to keyboard navigation.
- `'pointer'`: the highlight changed due to pointer hovering. The event may be a `MouseEvent`
  rather than a `PointerEvent`.
- `'none'`: the highlight changed for another reason, such as automatic highlighting while
  filtering, the item list changing, or the popup opening or closing.

onOpenChange.description: Event handler called when the menu is opened or closed.

onOpenChangeComplete.description: Event handler called after any animations complete when the menu is opened or closed.

open.description: Whether the menu is currently open.

orientation.description:
The visual orientation of the menu.
Controls whether roving focus uses up/down or left/right arrow keys.

triggerId.description:
ID of the trigger that the menu is associated with.
This is useful in conjunction with the `open` prop to create a controlled menu.
There's no need to specify this prop when the menu is uncontrolled (that is, when the `open` prop is not set).

closeDelay.description:
How long to wait before closing the menu that was opened on hover.
Specified in milliseconds.

Requires the `openOnHover` prop.

delay.description:
How long to wait before the menu may be opened on hover. Specified in milliseconds.

Requires the `openOnHover` prop.

disabled.description: Whether the component should ignore user interaction.

handle.description: A handle to associate the trigger with a menu.

nativeButton.description:
Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it
via the `render` prop.
Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

openOnHover.description: Whether the menu should also open when the trigger is hovered.

payload.description: A payload to pass to the menu when it is opened.

render.description:
Allows you to replace the component's HTML element
with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

align.description: Alignment of the menu against the trigger.

side.description: Which side of the trigger the menu opens on.

sideOffset.description: Gap in pixels between the trigger and the menu.

finalFocus.type: boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((closeType: InteractionType) => boolean | void | HTMLElement | null)
finalFocus.description:
Determines the element to focus when the menu is closed.

- `false`: Do not move focus.
- `true`: Move focus based on the default behavior (trigger or previously focused element).
- `RefObject`: Move focus to the ref element.
- `function`: Called with the interaction type (`mouse`, `touch`, `pen`, or `keyboard`).
  Return an element to focus, `true` to use the default behavior, or `false`/`undefined` to do nothing.

render.description:
Allows you to replace the component's HTML element
with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

color.description: danger marks destructive actions such as delete; the color is decided by the theme style.

closeOnClick.description: Whether to close the menu when the item is clicked.

disabled.description: Whether the component should ignore user interaction.

label.description:
Overrides the text used for keyboard text navigation and filtering.
Falls back to the rendered text when not provided.

nativeButton.description:

- `'input-blur'` when formatting (and clamping, if enabled) occurs on blur
- `'input-paste'` for paste interactions

It should be idempotent because OTP Field may normalize the same value more than once while
handling edits, storing state, and rendering controlled or uncontrolled values. Non-idempotent

If `autoSubmit` is enabled, it runs immediately before the owning form is submitted.

(close others / left / right / all, pin, refresh), and scroll buttons at both ends when there are too many.
It knows nothing about routing: tabs are data (`tabs` + `activeKey`), clicks and closes are handed back through callbacks, and you navigate yourself in the callback.
Together with `KeepAlive` the state of pages before closing can be kept around.

Keyboard: arrow keys move focus between tabs, Home / End go to the ends, Enter / Space switch, `Delete` closes, `Alt + Left/Right` reorders;
each action is announced with `role="status"`. Middle-click on a tab also closes it.

When the current tab is closed, it is called first, then `onActiveKeyChange` gives the new current item.

Determines if the popover enters a modal state when open.
- `true`: user interaction is limited to the popover: document page scroll is locked, and pointer interactions on outside elements are disabled.

- `'trap-focus'`: focus is trapped inside the popover, but document page scroll is not locked and pointer interactions outside of it remain enabled.

inside `<Popover.Popup>`. It can be visually hidden with your own CSS if needed, such as
Tailwind's `sr-only` utility.

Progress.description:
Progress indicator for a task that advances over time, drawn as a bar, a ring or a gauge.
`value` is the current amount within `min` / `max` (default 0–100); pass `null` for indeterminate progress (looping animation).
`type` picks line / circle / dashboard, `label` adds a caption, `showValue` shows the percentage; `color` / `size` / `radius` set its look.
For a static measurement within a range (disk usage, a score) use Meter; for a wait with no measurable progress use Spinner.

Theme style: accessibility (role / aria-valuenow) comes from Base UI, and the look of bar and ring is entirely in the theme style.
The ring is an SVG: a base circle plus an indicator circle, normalized with `pathLength=100`, so progress is just the percentage in stroke-dasharray (`--pc-value`).

value.description: Current value; pass null for indeterminate progress (looping animation).

The locale used by `Intl.NumberFormat` when formatting the value.
Defaults to the user's runtime locale.

QRCode.description:
QR code that encodes a string (usually a URL) as a scannable SVG image, sharp at any scale and rendered on the server too.
`value` is the text, `size` the side length in px, `icon` an image URL placed in the middle (raises the error level to H).
`status` shows loading / expired / scanned overlays; with "expired" a refresh button calls `onRefresh`, so a login QR can be renewed.
`color` / `bgColor` are functional scanning colors and do not follow the theme: black on white by default has the most reliable contrast (white background in dark themes too).
When `value` is too long for the largest version the error level allows, nothing is drawn.

Theme style: the encoding is implemented in qr.ts with no library dependency; the root carries `--qr-bg` / `--qr-size`, and when nothing can be drawn it is marked data-error.

Select.description:
Dropdown select that picks one value from a list of options; the trigger looks like Input (inside a Field it takes the Field's variant / size).
`options` is data: `{ value, label, disabled }` items or `{ label, options }` groups; `value` / `onValueChange` hold the selected value (a string).
The keyboard and type-ahead search work out of the box; the popup flips to stay in view and is placed by `side` / `align` / `sideOffset`.
To filter by typing use Combobox; for hierarchical options use Cascader or TreeSelect; for a few always-visible choices use RadioGroup or Segmented.

Theme style: behavior (keyboard, type-ahead search, collision flipping) comes from Base UI; the options, groups and selection indicator in the popup are decided by the theme style.

aria-label.description: Accessible name, when there is no visible label.

fullWidth.description: Fills the width of the parent.

invalid.description: When not inside a Field, mark it manually with invalid; inside a Field the Field's validation state decides.

options.description:

so the selected item's text can be read directly, and it is also easier to generate pages from data later.

A ref to imperative actions.

Call `preventUnmountOnClose()` in `onOpenChange` first, otherwise the select completes closing on its own.
Whether it leaves the DOM is decided by `keepMounted` on the portal.
- `close`: Closes the select imperatively when called.

Custom comparison logic used to determine if a select item value matches the current selected value. Useful when item values are objects without matching referentially.

Determines if the select enters a modal state when open.
- `true`: user interaction is limited to the select: document page scroll is locked and pointer interactions on outside elements are disabled.
- `false`: user interaction with the rest of the document is allowed.

On touch devices, a `true` modal blocks outside taps but leaves the page scrollable unless the popup spans nearly the full viewport width, matching native iOS behavior.

radius.description: Corner radius; the theme style decides when it is not passed.

text: one line of text high; circle: a perfect circle (avatar); rect: a block that fills its parent, sized by the parent.

Slider.description:
Slider for picking a number, or a range of numbers, by dragging a thumb along a horizontal track.
`value` / `onValueChange` hold a number for a single value or an array for a range (one thumb per value); `min` / `max` / `step` bound it.
`label` adds a caption, `showValue` shows the current value (formatted with `formatValue`, e.g. to add a unit); without a `label`, give it an `aria-label`.
Horizontal only for now. To type an exact number use NumberField.

Theme style: keyboard, touch and aria come from Base UI.

aria-label.description:
An accessible name is required when there is no `label` (the slider thumb is an `<input type="range">`; without a name screen readers cannot tell what it is).
Each thumb of a range slider is "name 1", "name 2"; use `thumbLabels` to name them yourself.

color.description: Semantic colour of the selected range and the thumb; the theme style picks the actual colours.

formatValue.description: How the current value is displayed (e.g. adding a unit); if omitted, Base UI's default number format is used. A range slider calls it once per value and joins them with –.

label.description: Text above the slider.

showValue.description: Shows the current value on the right of the text row (a range slider shows a – b).

size.description: Size step: the track's thickness and the thumb's size.

thumbLabels.description: Accessible name of each thumb, by index (e.g. ["Minimum price", "Maximum price"]); overrides the "name 1" / "name 2" default.

defaultValue.description:
The uncontrolled value of the slider when it's initially rendered.

To render a controlled slider, use the `value` prop instead.

disabled.description: Whether the slider should ignore user interaction.

form.description:
Identifies the form that owns the slider inputs.
Useful when the slider is rendered outside the form.

largeStep.description: The granularity with which the slider can step through values when using Page Up/Page Down or Shift + Arrow Up/Arrow Down.

locale.description:
The locale used by `Intl.NumberFormat` when formatting the value.
Defaults to the user's runtime locale.

max.description:
The maximum allowed value of the slider.
Should not be equal to min.

min.description:
The minimum allowed value of the slider.
Should not be equal to max.

minStepsBetweenValues.description: The minimum steps between values in a range slider.

name.description: Identifies the field when a form is submitted.

onValueChange.type: (value: number | readonly number[], eventDetails: SliderRootChangeEventDetails) => void
onValueChange.description:
Callback function that is fired when the slider's value changed.
Receives the new value as the first argument; the originating event is
available as `eventDetails.event`. The value is also reflected on
`eventDetails.event.target.value` for form integration.

The `eventDetails.reason` indicates what triggered the change:

- `'input-change'` when the hidden range input emits a change event (for example, via form integration)
- `'track-press'` when the control track is pressed
- `'drag'` while dragging a thumb
- `'keyboard'` for keyboard input
- `'none'` when the change is triggered without a specific interaction

onValueCommitted.type: (value: number | readonly number[], eventDetails: SliderRootCommitEventDetails) => void
onValueCommitted.description:
Callback function that is fired when a value change is committed.
Does not fire if the value did not change, or if the change was canceled.
**Warning**: This is a generic event, not a change event.

The `eventDetails.reason` indicates what triggered the commit:

- `'drag'` while dragging a thumb
- `'track-press'` when the control track is pressed
- `'keyboard'` for keyboard input
- `'input-change'` when the hidden range input emits a change event (for example, via form integration)
- `'none'` when the commit occurs without a specific interaction

step.description:
The granularity with which the slider can step through values. (A "discrete" slider.)
The `min` prop serves as the origin for the valid values.
We recommend (max - min) to be evenly divisible by the step.

thumbAlignment.description:
How the thumb(s) are aligned relative to `Slider.Control` when the value is at `min` or `max`:
- `center`: The center of the thumb is aligned with the control edge
- `edge`: The thumb is inset within the control such that its edge is aligned with the control edge
- `edge-client-only`: Same as `edge` but renders after React hydration on the client, reducing bundle size in return

thumbCollisionBehavior.description:
Controls how thumbs behave when they collide during pointer interactions.

- `'push'` (default): Thumbs push each other without restoring their previous positions when dragged back.
- `'swap'`: Thumbs swap places when dragged past each other.
- `'none'`: Thumbs cannot move past each other; excess movement is ignored.

value.description:
The value of the slider.
For range sliders, provide an array with one value per thumb.

Sortable.description:
Sortable list whose items the user reorders by dragging a handle, or with the keyboard (Space to pick up, arrow keys to move, Space to drop, Esc to cancel).
The caller owns the order: pass `items` (`{ id, label, content, disabled }`) and update them in `onReorder(ids, move)`, e.g. with the exported `arrayMove`.
`orientation` lays it out vertically (default) or horizontally; moves are announced to screen readers.
For cards moved between columns use Kanban.

Spinner: a spinning loading indicator for content that is still loading, with `size` and `color`.
It has `role="status"` and is announced as "Loading" unless you pass an `aria-label`.
For a loading button use Button's `loading`; for a placeholder of the content's shape use Skeleton; for an assistant

Split button: the main action on the left, with an arrow button attached on the right that opens a menu of related actions (corresponds to antd's `Dropdown.Button`).

`variant` / `color` / `size` / `radius` / `disabled` apply to both halves; give the arrow an accessible name with `menuLabel` (default "More actions").
For a single action use Button; for a menu without a main action use Menu.

disabled.description: Disables interaction.

Splitter.description:
Resizable split layout: several panels side by side (or stacked), with divider bars between them that the user drags, or moves with the keyboard (arrow keys, Home / End), to resize.
Put `Splitter.Panel` children inside (each with `defaultSize` / `min` / `max`, px or "30%"); `orientation` picks side by side or stacked.
Sizes are uncontrolled by default; pass `sizes` (px) with `onResize` to control them, or use `onResizeEnd` to persist them after a drag.
The last panel always fills the remaining space, so it absorbs any extra / missing space when the container grows or shrinks, and the other panels keep their proportions.

optional `prefix` / `suffix`) and an optional `description`. `Statistic.Countdown` counts down to a time.

Switch.description:
Switch: an on / off toggle for a setting that takes effect at once, with its label (`children`) and an optional `description`.
`checked` / `onCheckedChange` control it (`defaultChecked` for uncontrolled); clicking the text toggles it too.
For a choice confirmed later with a form submit use Checkbox; for a pressed / unpressed button use Toggle.

Theme style: structure and state conventions match Checkbox: <label> wraps "control + text", the state is on the control,
and the theme style reads it with :has().

children.description: Label text, to the right of the switch; without it only the switch is rendered, so give it an `aria-label`.

description.description: Secondary text under the label; clicking it toggles as well.

invalid.description: Mark invalid manually when not inside a Field; inside a Field it is decided by the Field's validation state.

checked.description:
Whether the switch is currently active.

defaultChecked.description:
Whether the switch is initially active.

To render a controlled switch, use the `checked` prop instead.

disabled.description: Whether the component should ignore user interaction.

form.description:
Identifies the form that owns the hidden input.
Useful when the switch is rendered outside the form.

id.description:
The id of the hidden input element.

When `nativeButton` is `true`, the id is applied to the root element.

inputRef.type: ((instance: HTMLInputElement | null) => void | (() => VoidOrUndefinedOnly)) | RefObject<HTMLInputElement | null>
inputRef.description: A ref to access the hidden `<input>` element.

name.description: Identifies the field when a form is submitted.

nativeButton.description:
Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it
via the `render` prop.
Set to `true` if the rendered element is a native button.

Tabs.description:
Tabs: switches between panels of content in the same place, one tab per panel.
Compose `Tabs.List` with `Tabs.Tab value="…"` and a matching `Tabs.Panel value="…"`; `value` / `onValueChange` control the
selected tab (`defaultValue` for uncontrolled). `variant` / `color` / `size` set the look, `fullWidth` stretches the tabs.
Arrow keys move between tabs. For a compact value picker use Segmented; for app-level open-page tabs use PageTabs.

Theme style: keyboard navigation, selected state and panel association all come from Base UI.

color.description: Colour of the selection indicator and highlight; the theme style picks the actual colours.

fullWidth.description: Stretches the list to the full width, the tabs sharing it equally.

variant.description: Visual variant: an underline / a solid slider / a soft slider; how each one looks is up to the theme style.

defaultValue.description:
The default value. Use when the component is not controlled.
When the value is `null`, no Tab will be active.

onValueChange.description:
Callback invoked when new value is being set.

The event `reason` is `'none'` for user-initiated changes, such as a click
or keyboard navigation; `'initial'` for the first automatic selection or
fallback in uncontrolled roots when `defaultValue` is omitted or
`undefined`, including when the implicit initial value is disabled or
missing; `'disabled'` for automatic fallback when the selected tab becomes
disabled in uncontrolled roots; or `'missing'` for automatic fallback when
the selected tab is removed, or when an explicit `defaultValue` never
matches a mounted tab in uncontrolled roots.

For automatic changes, the selected value can be `null` when no enabled Tab
is available as a fallback.

Automatic changes cannot be canceled; calling `eventDetails.cancel()` for
`'initial'`, `'disabled'`, or `'missing'` has no effect.
