Textarea.description:
Multi-line text input for longer free text (comments, descriptions); accepts native textarea props such as `rows` and `maxLength`.
`value` / `onValueChange` hold the text (a string); `autoSize` grows it with the content (optionally between `minRows` / `maxRows`), and `showCount` shows a character count.
Inside a Field it takes the Field's variant / size and validation state; outside, set `variant` / `size` / `invalid` yourself.
For a single line use Input; for a chat message box with send / attachments use Composer.

Theme style: the same Base UI Input, just rendered as a <textarea>; auto-grow writes the height as --ta-height and marks data-overflow beyond `maxRows`.

autoSize.type: boolean | { minRows?: number | undefined; maxRows?: number | undefined; }
autoSize.description:
Auto-grow with content: with `true` it is at least `rows` rows (default 2) with no upper limit; you can also pass `{ minRows, maxRows }`,
beyond `maxRows` the height is fixed and it scrolls inside. With auto-grow on, manual drag resizing is not possible.

fullWidth.description: Fills the width of the parent.

showCount.description: Show a character count below the input ("n / max" when there is a `maxLength`, changing color at the limit). Counted by `value.length`, consistent with native `maxLength`.

size.description:
Size step.
Inside a Field it defaults to the Field's.

variant.description:
`outline` is the regular input with a background / border, `filled` a grey fill (HeroUI v3's primary / secondary).
Inside a Field it defaults to the Field's.

defaultValue.description: The default value of the input. Use when uncontrolled.

onValueChange.type: (value: string, eventDetails: { reason: "none"; event: Event; cancel: () => void; allowPropagation: () => void; isCanceled: boolean; isPropagationAllowed: boolean; trigger: Element | undefined; }) => void
onValueChange.description: Callback fired when the `value` changes. Use when controlled.

value.description: The value of the input. Use when controlled.

ThreadList.description:
Conversation list (chat sidebar / conversation picker): each row is an icon, a title, a line of preview and supplementary info on the right.
The current conversation is written as `aria-current="true"` and highlighted; each row is a native button, usable with Tab / Enter / Space.
Overlong titles and previews are truncated, so rows fit in a narrow sidebar.

TimePanel.description:
Time selection panel: several scrollable columns of options (hours, minutes, optional seconds, and AM / PM for the 12-hour clock); clicking one sets it.
Each column is a listbox: up / down keys move between options, Home / End go to the ends, Enter selects; the selected item scrolls to the middle of its column.
When there is no value yet, clicking any item fills in the other parts starting from 00 (then clamped into the min / max range).

hour12.description: Show hours 12–11 with an AM / PM column (display only; the value stays 24-hour).

labels.description: Built-in texts to override (see its Labels type below); by default they follow the ConfigProvider locale.

max.description: Latest selectable time "HH:mm[:ss]"; later options are disabled.

min.description: Earliest selectable time "HH:mm[:ss]"; earlier options are disabled.

minuteStep.description: Interval between minute options, e.g. 15 for :00 / :15 / :30 / :45.

onChange.description: Called when an option is clicked / chosen with Enter, with the new time "HH:mm[:ss]" (24-hour, clamped into `min` / `max`).

seconds.description: Show a seconds column; the value then includes ":ss".

value.description: Current time "HH:mm[:ss]", null if none is selected.

TimePicker.description:
Time picker: a field-like trigger that opens a popup of scrollable hour / minute / (optional) second columns to pick a time of day.
`value` / `onValueChange` hold an "HH:mm" string ("HH:mm:ss" with `seconds`), 24-hour, or null; `hour12` only affects display and the panel, not the value.
`min` / `max` limit the range and `hourStep` / `minuteStep` / `secondStep` thin out the options.
Clicking an item changes that part and the value updates immediately (no need to click "OK"); "OK" only closes the panel; "Now" sets the current time (unavailable when outside min / max); `clearable` shows "Clear".
For a date use DatePicker; for the columns inline without a popup use TimePanel.

Theme style: the trigger reuses the Select look (slot is select-trigger), the popup is a Popover (marked data-picker) containing the TimePanel columns.

clearable.description: Show "Clear" at the bottom of the panel.

disabled.description: Disables interaction.

fullWidth.description: Fills the width of the parent.

value.description: Time "HH:mm" ("HH:mm:ss" when seconds are shown), 24-hour clock; null if none is selected.

copyable.description: Add a copy button after the text; without `text` it copies the displayed text, and after copying the button shows a check for about 2 seconds.

Toaster.description:
Toaster: shows the notifications raised with `toast` (`toast.success("Saved")`, `toast.loading(…)`, `toast.close(id)`).
Place it once at the app root; `position`, `layout` (list / stack), `limit` and `timeout` set where and how they appear,
`richColors` tints typed toasts in their color, `closeButton` and `icons` change the close button and the icons;
`toast.custom(render)` puts content of your own in a toast.
For a message that stays on the page use Alert; for a decision use Dialog / ConfirmDialog.

Theme style: toasts render in a Portal, so data-skein-theme must be set on <html> (ConfigProvider does it).

closeButton.description:
Show a close button on every toast (a toast's own `closeButton` overrides it); without one a toast closes by
its timeout, by swiping or from code (`toast.close(id)`).

icons.description: Icons by type, in place of the built-in ones (a toast's own `icon` overrides them).

layout.description: list: flat, one row per toast; stack: stacked, expands on hover or focus.

limit.description: Maximum number shown at once; extras are marked limited (the theme style decides how they collapse).

position.description: The corner the toasts appear in.

richColors.description:
Tint info / success / warning / danger toasts in their color (background, border and text), like Sonner's rich colors;
otherwise only the icon is colored. A toast's own `richColors` overrides it.

Toggle.description:
Toggle: a button that stays pressed or unpressed, such as Bold in a text editor.
`pressed` / `onPressedChange` control it (`defaultPressed` for uncontrolled); `variant` / `color` / `size` set its look,
`iconOnly` makes it square (give it an `aria-label`). Inside a ToggleGroup it takes the group's variant / color / size
and needs a `value`. For a setting switch use Switch; for a one-off action use Button.

Theme style: behavior comes from Base UI; it writes data-pressed when pressed.

color.description: Colour when pressed; inside a ToggleGroup the group's by default.

iconOnly.description: For icon-only use, with equal width and height.

size.description: Size step; inside a ToggleGroup the group's by default.

variant.description: Visual variant: transparent / outlined / always tinted; inside a ToggleGroup the group's by default.

defaultPressed.description:
Whether the toggle button is currently pressed.
This is the uncontrolled counterpart of `pressed`.

disabled.description: Whether the component should ignore user interaction.

nativeButton.description:
Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it
via the `render` prop.
Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

onPressedChange.type: (pressed: boolean, eventDetails: { reason: "none"; event: Event; cancel: () => void; allowPropagation: () => void; isCanceled: boolean; isPropagationAllowed: boolean; trigger: Element | undefined; }) => void
onPressedChange.description: Callback fired when the pressed state is changed.

pressed.description:
Whether the toggle button is currently pressed.
This is the controlled counterpart of `defaultPressed`.

Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

A unique string that identifies the toggle when used
inside a toggle group.

ToggleGroup.description:
ToggleGroup: a set of Toggles where one (or, with `multiple`, several) can be pressed, such as text alignment buttons.
`value` / `onValueChange` control it, and `value` is always an array of the pressed Toggles' `value`s; single-select by
default, clicking the pressed one again deselects it. `variant` / `color` / `size` pass down to the Toggles, `attached`
joins them, `orientation` stacks them. For a required single choice styled as a track use Segmented; in a form use RadioGroup.

Theme style: behavior comes from Base UI.

attached.description: Adjacent buttons sit flush together, with the border radius removed at the seams.

color.description: Pressed colour of the Toggles in the group.

size.description: Size of the Toggles in the group.

variant.description: Variant of the Toggles in the group; a Toggle's own `variant` wins.

defaultValue.description:
The pressed state of the toggle group represented by an array of
the values of all pressed toggle buttons.
This is the uncontrolled counterpart of `value`.

disabled.description: Whether the toggle group should ignore user interaction.

loopFocus.description:
Whether to loop keyboard focus back to the first item
when the end of the list is reached while using the arrow keys.

multiple.description:
When `false` only one item in the group can be pressed. If any item in
the group becomes pressed, the others will become unpressed.
When `true` multiple items can be pressed.

onValueChange.type: (groupValue: string[], eventDetails: { reason: "none"; event: Event; cancel: () => void; allowPropagation: () => void; isCanceled: boolean; isPropagationAllowed: boolean; trigger: Element | undefined; }) => void
onValueChange.description: Callback fired when the pressed states of the toggle group changes.

Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

The pressed state of the toggle group represented by an array of
the values of all pressed toggle buttons.
This is the controlled counterpart of `defaultValue`.

Toolbar.description:
Toolbar: a row of related controls (buttons, toggles, inputs) such as an editor's formatting bar.
Compose `Toolbar.Button`, `Toolbar.Group` and `Toolbar.Separator`; arrow keys move focus between the controls, so the
whole toolbar is a single tab stop. For a plain row of buttons with no keyboard grouping use ButtonGroup.

Theme style: behavior comes from Base UI; `Toolbar.Button` reuses Button's theme style.

loopFocus.description: If `true`, using keyboard navigation will wrap focus to the other end of the toolbar once the end is reached.

ToolCall.description:
Card for one tool call made by an AI assistant: the trigger is "status icon + tool name + status text", and when expanded it shows the input, the result (as JSON),
error details, and approve / reject buttons when approval is needed.
Pass `toolName`, `state` (input-streaming / input-available / output-available / output-error / requires-action), `input` / `output` (or `argsText` while streaming) and `errorText`;
for approval give `onApprove` / `onReject`. Expanded by default on error and when pending approval; `open` / `onOpenChange` control it.
To group several calls under one summary use ToolCallGroup; for the model's thinking steps use Reasoning.

Theme style: expand / collapse comes from Base UI's Collapsible; input and output are rendered with `CodeBlock`.

argsText.description: Already-formatted input text, used when arguments are streamed and the JSON is not yet complete; when given, `input` is not used.

children.description: Extra content in the panel, placed after the input / result.

errorText.description: Error details shown when state is output-error.

input.description: Tool input (any serializable value, shown as JSON; a string is shown as is).

labels.description: Built-in texts to override (see its Labels type below); by default they follow the ConfigProvider locale.

onApprove.description: Called when the user approves the call (state requires-action); the approve button is shown only when this is passed.

onReject.description: Called when the user rejects the call (state requires-action); the reject button is shown only when this is passed.

state.description:
State: input-streaming arguments are still being generated, input-available arguments are complete and executing, output-available a result is ready,
output-error an error occurred, requires-action the user must approve before continuing.
The panel is open by default on output-error and requires-action.

triggerPrefix.description: Text before the tool name on the trigger, e.g. "Used tool: ".

Whether the collapsible panel is initially open.

To render a controlled collapsible, use the `open` prop instead.

onOpenChange.description: Event handler called when the panel is opened or closed.

Whether the collapsible panel is currently open.

To render an uncontrolled collapsible, use the `defaultOpen` prop instead.

Allows you to replace the component's HTML element
with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

Tooltip.description:
Tooltip: a short text bubble shown when its trigger is hovered or focused, closed by Esc or leaving.
Wrap the trigger as `children` (a single element) and put the text in `content`; `side` / `align` / `sideOffset` place it,
`delay` / `closeDelay` time it, `arrow` adds a pointer. Wrap several in `Tooltip.Provider` to share the delay.
For interactive or richer content use Popover; for a preview of a link use PreviewCard.

Theme style: behavior (delay, focus, Esc to close, collision flipping) comes from Base UI, and the look is decided by the
theme style. The bubble is portaled to <body>, so theme style attributes must be on <html>.

arrow.description: Whether to include a small arrow pointing at the trigger element.

children.description: Trigger element; must be a single element that can take a ref and events (a button, a link, or your own component all work).

closeDelay.description: How long it stays after the pointer leaves (milliseconds).

delay.description: How long to hover before it appears (milliseconds); if omitted, the TooltipProvider's value is used.

side.description: Which side of the trigger it appears on; it flips when there isn't room.

sideOffset.description: Distance between the bubble and the trigger element (px).

defaultOpen.description:
Whether the tooltip is initially open.

To render a controlled tooltip, use the `open` prop instead.

disabled.description: Whether the tooltip is disabled.

onOpenChange.description: Event handler called when the tooltip is opened or closed.

open.description: Whether the tooltip is currently open.

trackCursorAxis.description: Determines which axis the tooltip should track the cursor on.

closeDelay.description: How long to wait before closing a tooltip. Specified in milliseconds.

delay.description: How long to wait before opening the tooltip on hover. Specified in milliseconds.

timeout.description:
Another tooltip will open instantly if the previous tooltip
is closed within this timeout. Specified in milliseconds.

Tour.description:
Guided tour: highlights one element on the page at a time, with a description card beside it and next / previous / finish.
`steps` lists `{ target, title, description, cover, side }` (a step without `target` is a centered intro card); `open` / `onOpenChange` show it,
`current` / `onCurrentChange` track the step, and `onFinish` fires on the last step's finish button. `mask`, `indicators` and `closable` tune the chrome; Esc closes.
The card flips to the other side automatically if it does not fit.
For a single hint next to an element use Popover or Tooltip.

Theme style: the card is a Popover anchored to the target element, and the mask's cut-out is a
highlight box that follows the target, darkening the surroundings with a huge box-shadow. Position and size are dynamic values, so the component writes no style:
a ref sets the target's rectangle as --tour-x / --tour-y / --tour-w / --tour-h on the root (pixels, without units).

closable.description: Close button in the top right; Esc also closes.

defaultOpen.description: Initial `open` when uncontrolled.

indicators.description: Step progress: dots for dots, count for text “2 / 5”, false for none.

labels.description: Button text (`prev`, `next`, `finish`, `close`), for switching languages.

mask.description: Mask with a cut-out highlight at the target; turn it off to leave only the card.

onCurrentChange.description: Called with the new `current`; pass `current` as well to control it.

onFinish.description: Called when the finish button on the last step is clicked (it closes afterwards).

onOpenChange.description: Called with the new `open`; pass `open` as well to control it.

open.description: Whether it is open, controlled (with `onOpenChange`).

steps.description:
The steps in order: `{ target, title, description, cover, side }`. `target` is a selector, an element, a ref or a
function returning the element; without one the step is a centered card.

cover.description: Image or any node above the title.

description.description: Body text of the step's card, explaining the highlighted element.

side.description: Which side of the target the card appears on, default bottom; flips to the other side automatically if it does not fit.

target.description: If omitted, it is a centered card with no highlight (good for an intro).

title.description: Heading of the step's card.

  indicators="count"
  steps={[{ title: "Welcome", description: "…" }, ...steps]} // a step without a target is centered
  labels={{ next: "Next step", finish: "Got it" }}
/>

Transfer.description:
Transfer: two lists side by side for choosing a subset of `items`: check items on one side and move them across with
the buttons in the middle. The value is the keys on the right (`value` / `onValueChange`); `searchable` adds a filter,
`oneWay` only moves to the right. For a few options use CheckboxGroup or a multiple Select.

aria-label.description: Accessible name, when there is no visible label.

disabled.description: Disables the whole transfer.

emptyText.description: Text when a list is empty (or the search has no results), default the locale's "No data".

items.description: All selectable items (both sides combined).

moveLabels.description: Accessible text of the two move buttons: [move to right, move back to left].

oneWay.description: Only allow moving from left to right; items on the right cannot be moved back (the right list has no checkboxes).

onValueChange.description: Called with the new keys after a move; pass `value` as well to control it.

searchable.description: Show a search box above each list, filtering by label; "select all" then only acts on the filtered items.

searchPlaceholder.description: Placeholder (and accessible name) of the search boxes, default the locale's "Search".

size.description: Size step: row height and font size.

titles.description: Titles of the left and right lists.

value.description: Keys of the items already on the right (the target list).

disabled.description: Disabled items cannot be selected, and are not selected by "select all".

key.description: Unique key; `value` holds the keys of the items on the right.

label.description: Text shown in the list; the search filters on it.

Tree.description:
Tree: a hierarchy of `nodes` (`{ id, label, children }`) that expand and collapse, for folders, categories or org charts.
Expanded / selected / checked are id arrays, controlled (`expanded`, `selected`, `checked` with their `on…Change`) or not;
`checkable` adds checkboxes, `draggable` + `onMove` reorder (see `moveTreeNode`), `onLoadChildren` loads lazily, `filter` searches.
Keyboard navigation follows the WAI-ARIA tree conventions. To pick a node in a form field use TreeSelect.

allowDrop.description: Filter whether it can be dropped here; positions that cannot be dropped on show no drop hint and do not trigger onMove.

aria-label.description: Accessible name, when there is no visible label.

aria-labelledby.description: Id of the element whose text names it.

block.description: The selected and hover background fills the whole row; if omitted it is decided by the theme style (antd by default only wraps the text).

checkable.description: Show a checkbox before each node; checking a parent also checks all available descendants, and when all descendants are checked the parent is checked automatically.

color.description: Semantic colour; the theme style picks the actual colours.

draggable.description: Allow dragging nodes to rearrange them (HTML5 drag and drop; on the keyboard use Alt + ↑ / ↓ to move one position among siblings).

emptyText.description: Content shown when the search has no matches; by default the locale's "No results".

expandOnClick.description: Clicking a row with children also expands / collapses it (like a file manager); set to false to expand only via the arrow.

filter.description:
Search term: when non-empty only matching nodes remain (along with their ancestors and the descendants of matching nodes), and it auto-expands to the matches;
cleared, it is restored. The expanded state is not rewritten, and nodes the user manually collapsed during the search stay collapsed until the search term changes.

filterMode.description: hide (default) hides non-matching nodes; highlight keeps all of them, only expanding to the matches and marking them.

filterNode.description: Custom match rule; if omitted it is a case-insensitive contains match (compares the label when the node label is a string, otherwise the id) and highlights the matching part of the text.

lines.description: Draws connecting lines between parents and children (like a directory structure); the expand arrow becomes a boxed plus / minus in the theme style.

nodes.description: The tree data: top-level nodes, each nesting its `children`.

onCheckedChange.description: Called with the new `checked`; pass `checked` as well to control it.

onExpandedChange.description: Called with the new `expanded`; pass `expanded` as well to control it.

onLoadChildren.description:
Called when expanding a lazy node that has no children yet. If it returns a Promise, the node shows a loading indicator while loading;
the consumer updates nodes after getting the data (fill in children, or remove lazy if there are no children).

onMove.description: Called on drop; Tree itself does not change nodes, use moveTreeNode(nodes, move) to get the new data and set it back.

onSelectedChange.description: Called with the new `selected`; pass `selected` as well to control it.

selected.description: Id of the currently selected node (single selection).

disabled.description: Disables interaction.

icon.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | ((state: TreeNodeState) => ReactNode)
icon.description: Icon before the label, not rendered if omitted; pass a function to swap the icon by node state.

id.description: Unique id across the whole tree; used by selection, expansion and callbacks.

label.description: Content of the node's row.

lazy.description: Has child nodes that are not loaded yet: shows the expand arrow and calls onLoadChildren on first expand.

examples.title: Usage
Async loading
examples.code:
<Tree
  nodes={nodes}
  onLoadChildren={async (id) => {
    const children = await fetchChildren(id);
    setNodes((list) => setChildren(list, id, children));
  }}
/>
// in nodes: { id: "projects", label: "projects", lazy: true }

TreeSelect.description:
Tree select: the trigger looks like Select, and the popup holds a `Tree`. Single selection picks a node on click,
multiple selection checks boxes; supports search and async loading.
For flat data use Select; for two or three levels picked one level at a time use Cascader.

aria-label.description: Accessible name, when there is no visible label.

clearable.description: Show a clear button when there is a value.

disabled.description: Disables interaction.

emptyText.description: Content shown when the search has no matches, default the locale's "No results".

fullWidth.description: Fills the width of the parent.

maxTagCount.description: Maximum number of tags shown in the trigger; the rest collapse into "+N".

multiple.description: Multiple selection: each node has a checkbox, and checking a parent checks all available leaves beneath it.

nodes.description: The tree data: top-level nodes, each nesting its `children`.

onLoadChildren.description: Called when expanding a lazy node that has no children yet; if it returns a Promise the node shows a spinner while loading.

onValueChange.description: Called with the new `value`; pass `value` as well to control it.

placeholder.description: Text shown while empty, default the locale's "Select".

searchable.description: Show a search box at the top of the overlay: after typing, the tree keeps only matching nodes (along with ancestors).

searchPlaceholder.description: Placeholder (and accessible name) of the search box, default the locale's "Search".

size.description: Size step, as on Select; inside a Field it defaults to the Field's.

value.description:
Id of the selected node (nodes at any level can be selected).
Ids of selected leaf nodes (parents are derived from descendants and are not included).

variant.description: Visual variant of the trigger, as on Select; inside a Field it defaults to the Field's.

disabled.description: Disables interaction.

id.description: Unique id across the whole tree; this is what `value` holds.

label.description: It is what the trigger displays, so it must be text.

lazy.description: Has child nodes that are not loaded yet: calls onLoadChildren on first expand.

examples.title: Basic
examples.code:
import { TreeSelect } from "@skeinui/ui";

<TreeSelect aria-label="City" nodes={[{ id: "zj", label: "Zhejiang", children: [...] }]} />

Typing.description:
Typing: a "the assistant is typing" indicator shown while a chat reply has not started yet.
`variant` picks dots, a pulse, a spinner or a skeleton; it has `role="status"` and screen readers read `label` once.
For general loading use Spinner; for animated text while a reply streams use ShimmerText.

Theme style: the drawn dots / ring / placeholder bars are aria-hidden decoration; the animation is in the theme style and
stops under "reduced motion".

label.description: Text read by screen readers (the root is `role="status"`); by default the locale's "Assistant is typing".

variant.description: dots: three dots (default), pulse: a pulsing dot, spinner: a spinning ring, skeleton: an avatar plus a few lines of placeholder text.

examples.title: Variants
examples.code:
import { Typing } from "@skeinui/ui";

<Typing />
<Typing variant="pulse" />
<Typing variant="spinner" />
<Typing variant="skeleton" />

Typography.description:
Content typography container: headings, paragraphs, lists, quotes, code, links, dividers and tables inside automatically get suitable font sizes and spacing,
for displaying articles, documentation and content rendered from Markdown. Just write native elements inside, no need to wrap each in Title / Paragraph.

as.description: The container element; native headings, paragraphs, lists, quotes, code, links and tables inside it get suitable typography.

examples.title: Copyable
examples.code:
<Text copyable>copy me</Text>
<Text copyable={{ text: "sk-live-…", onCopy: () => toast("Copied") }}>sk-live-••••</Text>

Upload.description:
Upload: a file picker (a button, or a drag-and-drop `variant="dropzone"`) plus the list of files with progress and errors.
It does not upload anything itself: `onFilesAdded` hands you the chosen files, you upload them and pass their state
back in `files` (status, progress, error); `onRemove` / `onRetry` act on one file. `accept` / `multiple` filter the choice.

aria-label.description: Accessible name, when there is no visible label.

disabled.description: Disables selecting and dropping files.

files.description: Files that are selected / uploading / uploaded, maintained by the consumer; each row's `status` is uploading / done / error.

hint.description: Description under the main text, e.g. format and size limits.

icon.description: Icon of the trigger area; the built-in upload icon if omitted.

multiple.description: Allow selecting / dropping several files at once; otherwise only the first is passed to `onFilesAdded`.

onFilesAdded.description: Called after files are selected or dropped in; the component does not upload, the consumer takes the File, sends the request itself and updates files.

onRemove.description: Click the remove button of a file row; files being uploaded can be cancelled the same way.

onRetry.description: Click the retry button of a failed file; if omitted, retry is not shown.

removeLabel.description: Accessible text of the remove button in a file row, default "Remove".

retryLabel.description: Accessible text of the retry button in a failed file row, default "Retry".

title.description: Main text of the trigger area, dropzone defaults to "Click or drag files here", button defaults to "Select file".

variant.description: dropzone is a drag-and-drop area, button is just a button.

error.description: Reason shown when status is error.

id.description: Unique id chosen by the consumer; passed to `onRemove` / `onRetry`.

name.description: Field name, for native form submission.

size.description: Size in bytes, used to display the size.

examples.title: Usage
File states
examples.code: files={[{ id, name, size, status: "done" | "uploading" | "error", progress, error }]}

Watermark.description:
Watermark: overlays repeated semi-transparent text or an image on its `children` without blocking the mouse, e.g. to mark confidential pages with the user's name.
`content` is the text (an array for several lines) or `image` an image URL; `rotate`, `gap`, `offset`, `width` / `height` and `font` tune the pattern.
`antiTamper` (on by default) restores the layer if it is removed or edited in devtools. The default text color follows the content's text color, so it works in light and dark.

Theme style: the pattern is a bitmap drawn with canvas, used as the watermark layer's background;
it is a dynamic value, so the component writes no style: a ref sets it as --wm-image / --wm-w / --wm-h / --wm-ox / --wm-oy / --wm-z on the watermark layer,
and the theme style handles position and background. It is redrawn when the colour theme or theme style switches (html attribute changes), so the default text color works in both light and dark.

antiTamper.description: Automatically restore the watermark layer when it is removed or its attributes are changed.

content.description: Watermark text; an array means multiple lines.

font.description: Text style of a text watermark: `{ color, fontSize, fontWeight, fontStyle, fontFamily }`. Without `color` it takes the content's text color faded to 15%, which works in light and dark.

image.description: Image URL; when given, the image is drawn (text is no longer drawn). Use a same-origin or CORS-enabled image, otherwise it cannot be drawn.

width.description: Width and height (pixels) of each watermark. For text, sized by the text if omitted; images default to 120 × 64.

zIndex.description: z-index of the watermark layer (above the content but below overlays).

color.description: Text color; if omitted, the current text color of the content area is used, faded to 15% opacity (works in both light and dark).

fontFamily.description: CSS font family; the content area's font if omitted.

examples.title: Custom style
examples.code:
<Watermark
  content="Draft"
  rotate={-10}
  gap={[40, 40]}
  font={{ fontSize: 20, fontWeight: 700, color: "rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.18)" }}
>…</Watermark>

WebPreview.description:
Web preview: sandboxed iframe + address bar (Enter to navigate) + reload + open in a new tab.
Content can be an address (`src`, only http(s) is accepted) or a piece of HTML (`html`, using srcdoc). The iframe by default only enables scripts and forms and is cross-origin,
and while loading there is a screen-reader-readable status below the address bar. The browser's back / forward cannot get a cross-origin iframe's history, so they are not provided.

editable.description:
The address bar is editable, default true; read-only when false. Enter navigates (an address without a protocol gets `https://`;
anything but http(s), such as `javascript:` / `data:` / `file:`, is rejected), Esc restores the current address.

height.description: Height of the preview area (px), default 360.

html.description:
A complete HTML document rendered in the iframe via srcdoc (e.g. code generated by a model). Pass either `src` or `html`.
With `html` the toolbar shows the title instead of an address and has no open-in-new-tab link.

labels.description: Built-in texts to override (see its Labels type below); by default they follow the ConfigProvider locale.

onNavigate.description: Triggered after the user navigates from the address bar.

sandbox.description:
Sandbox of the iframe. Default `allow-scripts allow-forms`: scripts and forms can run, but it is cross-origin (cannot read the host's cookies / storage),
cannot open popups and cannot navigate the host. Giving `allow-scripts` + `allow-same-origin` is the same as having no sandbox, so add it only when the content is fully trusted.

src.description: Address to load in the iframe (only http(s) is accepted); shown in the address bar. Pass either `src` or `html`.

title.description: Name of the iframe (for screen readers), default "Preview".

invalid.description: Hint when the address is not http(s), default "Only http(s) addresses can be previewed".

loading.description: Screen reader text while loading, default "Loading".

open.description: Open in a new tab, default "Open in new tab".

title.description: Name of the iframe when `title` is not given.

examples.title: Usage
examples.code:
import { WebPreview } from "@skeinui/ui";

<WebPreview src="https://example.com" title="Example" height={300} />
